newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Cisneros to buy Argentine TV group.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Cisneros to buy Argentine TV group.

text.p: The Cisneros Group of Companies, one of Latin America's leading business conglomerates, said late Thursday it had signed a letter of intent to buy Argentine cable programmer Imagen Satelital for $109 million, including $9 million in debt.

Subject to final documentation, Miami-based Cisneros Television Group (CTG) will own Imagen Satelital, Argentina's top cable programmer with six owned channels, distribution rights to nine others, and a large film library.

"The Cisneros Group's resources will propel Imagen Satelital into the international arena as the premier provider of programming in Latin America," Imagin president and founder Alberto Gonzalez said in a press release.

"For some time now, I have known that for Imagen to grow and become a an international player, we needed to partner with a blue chip, world class media concern," he added. Gonzalez and his partners will continue in senior management.
The purchase continues the family-owned Cisneros Group's expansion into Latin American media and entertainment.
Group affiliates include Venevision, the largest producer of Spanish-language television programming in South America, and Venevision International, which distributes programming around the world.

"The Imagen Satelital agreement will greatly strengthen the foundation of the Cisneros Television Group and will fit ideally into the Cisneros Group of Companies," said Group Chairman Gustavo Cisneros. In 1996, the group had revenues of $3.2 billion.

Cisneros's broadcasting interests extend to a founding stake in Galaxy Latin America which delivers Hughes Electronic Corp's satellite service DIRECTV to Latin America, as well as significant holdings in U.S. Spanish-language network Univision, Chilevision in Chile and CCN of Trinidad and Tobago.
Violy, Byorum and Partners Llc acted as financial advisors for the deal.
